info.title: Mind2Flow API
info.description:
Public REST API for building, managing and executing AI agents, multi-agent crews, devices, custom Python tools and scheduled tasks on the Mind2Flow platform.

Authenticate with a REST API key (created in the dashboard under Developers → API) sent as `x-api-key: rest_...` or `Authorization: Bearer rest_...`.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Create, manage and execute AI agents

tags.name: Tools
tags.description: Custom Python tools and sandbox execution

tags.name: Analysis
tags.description: Operational figures, conversation reading and search, LLM analysis and configuration diagnostics for your agents. Scope: agents:read. Organization-wide reads additionally require the TENANT or ADMIN role and are confined to your own customer.

tags.name: Artifacts
tags.description: Documents built from typed blocks — reports, test runs, prompt changes — whose figures are resolved from the database by the server, never typed by a model. Versioned; shareable by a public link that hides customer details by default. Scopes: agents:read / agents:write.

tags.name: Panels
tags.description: For external panels (a CRM, an inbox): subscribe to a WhatsApp device's traffic through a signed webhook and send through it. Available when panels are enabled on the server.

tags.name: Voice
tags.description: Phone calls with your agents (Twilio ConversationRelay, on your own Twilio account). Connect Twilio and pick a number once in the console (AI Agents → agent → Voice); then place calls, change the voice or greeting, pause the line and read calls here. Billed at 1 credit per 15 s of AI talk time (see /voice/pricing); Twilio bills minutes and numbers to your Twilio account. Scopes: agents:read / agents:write.

tags.name: Knowledge
tags.description: GraphOS temporal knowledge graph: sources, ingestion, hybrid query and graph exploration. Scopes: knowledge:read / knowledge:write. Requires an OpenAI key on the account (BYOK) for ingestion and query.

get.summary: Aggregated operational figures for an agent
get.description: Volume, distinct people, conversation depth, hour-of-day distribution (UTC), channels, response-time percentiles and errors, over a date range. Computed from the database, so these figures are exact. Read `notes` back to whoever sees the numbers: it reports when people could not be counted (activities recorded before sender tracking shipped carry no sender id), when messages came from the agent's own scheduled tasks, and when the range held more rows than were read.

get.summary: Find which conversations mention given terms
get.description: Per term: how many DISTINCT CONVERSATIONS and how many messages matched, plus the session ids. Per matching conversation: which terms hit, with snippets. Several terms in one call, because "how many people asked for each of these ten products" is one question. Matching is literal substring: case-insensitive but ACCENT-SENSITIVE, so "credito" does not match "crédito" — pass both spellings as separate terms. Per-term counts double-count a conversation that matched two terms; use `matches.length` for the de-duplicated number.

post.summary: Ask an arbitrary question of an agent's conversations
post.description:
You supply the question AND the fields you want back, so "which products did people ask for", "did this end in a sale" and "what went wrong" are all this one endpoint. Conversations are read in batches, so a month that would never fit in one context window is a handful of passes. Returns a value per conversation plus a frequency table per field.

COST: this is the only endpoint here that spends. It runs an LLM on YOUR account's own key (or the trial key while that is active) and answers 402 when the account has neither — it is never billed to anyone else. Keep `maxConversations` to what the question needs.

Values are extracted by a model reading text, so they can be wrong or missed. Hard figures belong to /summary, which is computed from the database.

parameters.description: Agent id, or "all" for every agent you own

question.description: What to determine about each conversation, in plain language.

fields.description: The values you want back per conversation, up to 8. Each becomes a column and a frequency table.

get.summary: Connected apps, and whether the wiring works
get.description: The Composio toolkits the agent is configured to use, the account pinned per app, how many actions are selected, the account's live connections, and `issues` — where configuration and reality disagree (pinned to an account that no longer exists, connected but not ACTIVE, apps with no actions selected). When Composio cannot be reached, `connections` is null and `notes` says the check did not run. That is not the same as "disconnected". `issues` holds real problems only.

get.summary: How the agent can be reached, and whether each way works
get.description:
Input and output channel, the API endpoint, the assigned WhatsApp device with its number and the date of the last inbound message, and the shared link with its active flag, expiry and request count. `issues` lists what is broken.

WhatsApp is probed LIVE: `whatsapp.liveState` is "open" when connected. When the probe cannot run, `liveCheck` is "failed" and `notes` says so; the stored `isConnectedFlag` can be stale, so weigh it against `lastInboundAt`.

get.summary: What the agent's app actions actually did
get.description:
Every tool call the agent made — create a CRM contact, add a sheet row, book an event, search its knowledge — with the app's real answer: ok or the error, and the ids created. Aggregated per action with error rate, top errors and recent ids, plus the latest errors.

"ok" means the app's API accepted the call, not what the app did afterwards. Calls are recorded from the day action logging was deployed: `loggingSince` says where the record starts. When the account keeps content out of the database, arguments and error texts are redacted; counts and ids are exact.

post.summary: Play test conversations against the agent, for real
post.description:
Runs each case, turn by turn, on a temporary copy of the agent (deleted afterwards): replies are not delivered to any channel and do not count in the agent's figures, but its connected apps run for real. A language model on your key grades each answer. Returns at once with the id of a `test_run` artifact that fills in as cases finish; poll `GET /artifacts/{id}` until `status` is `done`.

`{{name}}`, `{{phone}}` and `{{email}}` in a turn take the values of `identity`. Up to 15 cases of up to 5 turns.

post.summary: Create an artifact
post.description:
Either your own blocks and data sources, or a template. Sources are run on the server as you (same services and ownership checks as the Analysis endpoints) and stored with the artifact; blocks point into them with `source: { ref, path }`. An `analysis` source runs an LLM on your key.

With `parentId`, the artifact becomes a new version of that one.

put.summary: Subscribe a panel to a device
put.description: From now on every message the device receives or sends (agent replies included), every delivery status and every connection change is POSTed to `url`. Each delivery carries `X-M2F-Timestamp`, `X-M2F-Event`, `X-M2F-Delivery` (stable across retries — use it as an idempotency key) and `X-M2F-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<timestamp>.<raw body>" with the returned secret>`. A device has one subscription; calling this again replaces the URL. Messages are delivered at least once — after a gap (a restart, or the first event of a device) the missed ones are recovered and sent with `replayed: true`, so deduplicate on `message.id`. Status and connection events are not recovered.

url.description: Public https URL of the panel

OperationSummary.description: Exact figures computed from the database. `notes` carries the caveats that must travel with them.

agentName.description: The agent these results belong to; null for "all".

messages.description: Incoming plus successful replies. Failed replies are in `errors`.

scheduledRuns.description: Incoming messages fired by the agent's own scheduled tasks, not by a person.

unattributedMessages.description: Messages with no sender id; see `notes`.

depth.description: Agent replies per person, as the raw histogram.

truncated.description: Cut to fit the budget: the opening and the ending are kept.

omittedMessages.description: Messages left out of the middle when truncated.

agentName.description: The agent these results belong to; null for "all".
The agent these results belong to; null for "all".

terms.description: Per term. A conversation matching two terms is counted in both.

matches.description: De-duplicated: every conversation that matched at least one term.

ConversationAnalysis.description: Values extracted by a language model: they can be wrong or missed.

agentName.description: The agent these results belong to; null for "all".

aggregates.description: Per field: value → how many distinct conversations gave it.

ArtifactBlock.description: One of: heading {text, level}, text {markdown}, callout {tone, text}, kpis {items}, table {columns, rows | source}, chart {kind, x, y, rows | source}, excerpt {contact, messages}, test_results {cases}, diff {before, after}, divider. See the SDK types for every field.

template.description: Instead of blocks: a report the server composes. Needs agentId; from/to default to the previous calendar month.

status.description: ready | running | done | interrupted | failed | archived

data.description: `sources`: each resolved source ({ ok, status, payload | message }); `sourceSpecs`: what was asked for.

connections.description: Null when Composio could not be reached — not the same as disconnected.

isConnectedFlag.description: Stored flag; can be stale. Prefer `liveState`.

liveState.description: Live state from the connection server: "open" is connected, "not_found" means the instance no longer exists (number not linked). Null when the probe did not run.

invalid_at.description: In the future = validity window end; in the past = superseded

secret.description: Verifies X-M2F-Signature. Stable for the device.

message.description: Text, or the caption of a media message

PanelEvent.description: Body of a webhook delivery. Exactly one of message / status / connection is present, per `type`.

omitted.description: True when the file was too large to embed

url.description: Instead of base64, for a message that was sent by URL

replayed.description: True on a message recovered after a gap instead of seen live. It may repeat one already delivered: deduplicate on message.id.

raw.description: The gateway's original payload, without media bytes

enabled.description: false = paused: callers hear that the number is not available

voiceName.description: Catalog name, null for a voice outside the catalog

voice.description: Catalog id (el-cristina), name (Cristina) or an ElevenLabs voice id

phoneNumber.description: E.164 number already in your Twilio account; creates the line if the agent has none

callStatus.description: Twilio final state: completed, no-answer, busy, failed, canceled

aiSeconds.description: Talk time with the AI (what is billed)

outcome.description: solicita-cita, informacion, recado, transferida, queja, sin-interes — or the Twilio state (no-answer, busy, failed) when the call never connected

message.description: Message sent to the agent on each run
